inputKind: Public researcher-authored source summaries and limitations from fifteen retained research slices. Not full documents, the entire legacy corpus or all NSE companies.
lineageLimitation: Separate namespace summaries may cite one document. Repeated URLs are not independent corroboration.

documents.title: Philippines accepts BrahMos USD 374,962,800 price proposal
documents.text: Reports exact accepted price proposal in DND notice of award before contract signature. Original notice instrument not retained; USD amount is award-stage reporting, not a bank receipt.

documents.title: DND signs PHP 18.9 billion BrahMos acquisition contract
documents.text: Government news agency reports signed DND–BrahMos contract, PHP 18.9 billion and three batteries including training and logistics. Indexed original article retained; direct URL retrieval redirected to unrelated Facebook content and is recorded as failed. Signed instrument and exact currency schedule not opened.

documents.title: DND confirms another BrahMos batch en route
documents.text: First deliveries occurred in April 2024; another batch was en route on 23 April 2025. No complete three-battery acceptance asserted. Indexed original article retained; direct URL response was unrelated Facebook content. En route is not delivered or accepted.

documents.title: BrahMos: inception, partners and 2014 IGA extension
documents.text: Company identifies DRDO India and JSC Military Industrial Corporation NPO Mashinostroyenia Russia as partners;1998 formation and 2014 indefinite IGA extension. Undated company history accessed 7 October 2026; 50.5/49.5 authorised-capital ratio is inception history, not audited current beneficial ownership or paid-in capital.

documents.title: MoD signs contract with Airbus for 56 C-295MW aircraft
documents.text: Airbus Defence and Space S.A., Spain, is the contracting vendor; 16 flyaway and 40 Indian-built aircraft; offset contract also signed. The release does not state the contract price, Tata receipt split or offset settlement.

documents.title: Airbus military aircraft orders and deliveries to 30 June 2026
documents.text: India has 56 C295 orders and 16 deliveries in the manufacturer cumulative table. Monthly snapshot not proof of a post-June delivery. In-operation column is not mapped to unit readiness or deployment.

documents.title: TASL and Airbus inaugurate C295 final assembly line
documents.text: Public final assembly line inauguration, six aircraft already delivered; first local rollout planned September 2026. Inauguration and target dates do not establish that the first local delivery occurred.

documents.title: Airbus delivers first C295 to India
documents.text: Manufacturer announces first delivery to IAF on 13 September 2023. Manufacturer announcement; no acceptance certificate or payment receipt retained.

documents.title: C-295 Indian manufacture: project cost and named Tata consortium
documents.text: INR 21,935 crore total project cost; Indian Aircraft Contractor is TASL-led consortium of TASL and TCS; same September 2021 contract. Project cost is not a TASL award or receipt; consortium participation is not a new legal JV or ownership percentage.

documents.title: Ministry of Defence Year End Review 2022: DRDO and BrahMos export identity
documents.text: Official ministry spells out DRDO and identifies BrahMos Aerospace Private Limited (BAPL) as its joint-venture company signing the Philippine Department of National Defence export contract. Used to document exact institutional/vendor identity, not current shareholder percentages, exporter receipts or the Philippine contract price.

documents.title: MQ-9B deliveries expected 2029–2030
documents.text: Officials describe prospective delivery 51–72 months after signature and initial payment, expected 2029–2030. Conditional forecast, not proof of initial payment or actual delivery. Unnamed-source approximate price is not substituted for unpublished definitive contract price.

documents.title: DSCA Transmittal 24-07: India MQ-9B proposed sale
documents.text: Original government publication reproduces 1 February 2024 Congressional notification: national funds,31 aircraft, estimated USD 3.99 billion, principal General Atomics Aeronautical Systems. Proposal-stage estimate, not signed contract value or disbursement; publication in January 2025 is not a new January 2025 approval.

documents.title: Defence Year End Review 2024: MQ-9B contracts
documents.text: Ministry confirms October 2024 acquisition of 31 and a separate Indian logistics contract with General Atomics Global India Pvt Ltd. No final contract price, advance payment, delivery acceptance or corporate parentage is supplied in this paragraph.

documents.title: India and US sign 31 MQ-9B contract and separate logistics agreement
documents.text: Reports 15 October signature: MoD–US Government acquisition contract and MoD–General Atomics Global India Private Limited logistics contract. Public broadcaster report of signing; executed contract and price schedule not retained.

documents.title: AEL: completed acquisition of 27.26% NDTV from Roys
documents.text: RRPR acquired 27.26% at INR 342.65 per share; block deal completed December 30, exchange settlement formalities noted; legal CIN of NDTV stated. Cash consideration price is not an independently reconciled seller bank receipt.

documents.title: AMG Media Networks statement on NDTV transition
documents.text: Acquirer says AMNL controlled 64.71% through subsidiaries and describes investment in the newsroom and a friendly transition. Company strategy and description of the transition are attributed statements, not an independent editorial-independence assessment.

documents.title: AEL: VCPL exercises RRPR warrants and announces NDTV open offer
documents.text: Identifies AEL → AMNL → VCPL ownership; 1,990,000 RRPR warrants for INR 19,900,000; proposed acquisition of up to 26% NDTV. The exercise notice and offer are dated stages, not proof that the maximum offer was fully accepted.

documents.title: DOJ emails: Puri’s India economic pitch and interactions
documents.text: Reports published email exchanges; distinguishes the retired diplomat’s business pitch from later ministerial office. Reporting and the opened public transcription support correspondence only. No bank transfer, completed investment or criminal participation by Puri is established.

documents.title: Published copy of DOJ release EFTA00688056–57: India internet pitch
documents.text: Puri pitches Indian internet opportunities to Epstein and Reid Hoffman. This is correspondence proposing engagement, not a payment instrument. DOJ file URL returned age-verification HTML; that failure is retained and no original PDF retrieval is claimed. Opened transcription corroborated by linked reporting in The Indian Express and The News Minute. The email’s third-party investment figures and forecasts are not treated as verified transactions by Epstein, Puri or Hoffman. No victim-identifying information is reproduced in structured data.

documents.title: Puri acknowledges meetings and denies connection to wrongdoing
documents.text: Reports Puri saying he met Epstein three or four times through IPI and had no connection to wrongdoing or crimes. Reuters direct URL returned HTTP 401; opened indexed Reuters text retained. His explanation is a response, not independently adjudicated fact.

documents.title: KPMG forensic review of IPI transactions involving Epstein-linked entities
documents.text: Five donations USD 650,000 and one airfare reimbursement USD 14,158.88 identified in scoped financial review; no IPI payments to Epstein or 56 listed entities identified. Consulting/advisory engagement, expressly not an audit/attestation or assurance opinion. Relied on IPI-provided information; public-record entity affiliations not independently verified. Review covers 2010-01-01 through 2020-10-31. The earliest retained donation is check 2011-10-11 / ledger 2011-10-13, within atlas window. The report bears a client-confidential header but was voluntarily published in full by IPI. No nonpublic IRS Schedule B or bank records were accessed by this project.

documents.title: IPI probity review: conflicts, donor policy and legal boundaries
documents.text: Counsel found no identified legal prohibition on receiving donations or evidence of personal benefit to Epstein; criticises undisclosed personal loan judgment. Commissioned legal review is not a criminal acquittal or exhaustive investigation. The report’s assumptions and limited scope are preserved.

documents.title: IPI final report identifies Hardeep Singh Puri’s ICM role
documents.text: Identifies former Indian diplomat Puri as secretary-general of IPI’s Independent Commission on Multilateralism. Institutional role does not establish control of donor funds, salary funding source or receipt of Epstein-related funds. Exact role end-date is not asserted.

documents.title: IPI publishes forensic and probity reviews; explains remedial policy
documents.text: IPI reports resignation, commissioning of reviews and direction to donate equivalent funds to programmes supporting survivors. Board pledge/direction is not proof that equivalent donations were subsequently paid. Headline statement rounds airfare to USD 14,158; underlying KPMG report USD 14,158.88 controls.

documents.title: NDTV annual report FY 2025–26 and audited standalone financial statements
documents.text: Rights issue proceeds INR 3,964.98 million; RRPR 67,473,129 shares 59.80% and VCPL 10,402,138 shares 9.22% in standalone note 14; legal closure and continuing SEBI matter distinguished. Original 14 MB PDF kept in /workspace/.cache/atlas-institutions with SHA 256 receipt; fulltext, exact page excerpts and shareholding PNG tracked. Standalone note 14 and promoter aggregate 69.02% are used. Consolidated note 14 prints VCPL 9.21% in one table despite the same 10,402,138 shares; standalone table and consolidated promoter table print 9.22%. No silent averaging. Legal case status is the issuer’s May 2026 disclosure; underlying 2025 orders were not independently retrieved.

documents.title: NDTV: ownership, direct holdings and founder resignations
documents.text: Records 1,75,77,676 shares acquired from the two named founders; RRPR 56.45%, VCPL 8.27% and founders 5% combined. Original URL returned HTTP 403; full relevant ownership table and founder DINs read through indexed original-file fetch and retained in ndtv-completion-indexed-excerpt.json. Unrelated later annexures/contact details omitted.

documents.title: VCPL notice: equalising payment for accepted NDTV open-offer shares
documents.text: VCPL says initial consideration on 5,330,792 accepted shares completed December 15, 2022; promises an additional INR 48.65/share by February 28, 2023 to match the founders’INR 342.65/share price. Original URL returned HTTP 403; opened indexed original-file OCR retained in ndtv-equalisation-indexed.json. Repeated paragraph 5 corroborates amount/deadline despite imperfect OCR. This notice is a payment commitment; actual additional-payment settlement or shareholder bank receipts were not independently retrieved.

documents.title: NDTV: RRPR instructs bankers to return warrant deposit
documents.text: Founders say SEBI clearance is needed and RRPR instructed return of INR 1,99,00,000. Original URL returned HTTP 403; opened indexed original PDF text retained. An instruction to return is not a verified bank refund.

documents.title: NDTV: founders respond to warrant exercise notice
documents.text: Records the INR 1.99 crore notice-stage deposit and founders’ lack-of-consent response. Original URL returned HTTP 403; opened indexed original PDF text is retained in indexed-fetch.json.

documents.title: Norway hearings and separate police probes after Epstein disclosures
documents.text: Reports ongoing Norwegian investigations, Roed-Larsen’s denial of wrongdoing and separate parliamentary inquiry. Police investigation is not conviction. This Norwegian follow-up is not a finding against Puri, IPI’s Indian work or an Indian recipient. It does not change the scoped 2020 review into a global exoneration.

documents.title: Supreme Court extends temple and trusts special-audit deadline
documents.text: Reports a further audit deadline and requirement to file a compliance report. Underlying extension order and completed special-audit report not retrieved. Targeted later-outcome search through 2026 did not locate a final publicly accessible report; this is a corpus gap, not proof audit never occurred.

documents.title: Supreme Court: Sri Marthanda Varma v State of Kerala
documents.text: Upholds shebaitship succession, establishes committee management and directs 25-year audit and preservation of temple assets. Historical disputes and pre-2011 legislation are context; an audit direction is not a final quantified misappropriation finding.

documents.title: Supreme Court: Temple Trust audit clarification
documents.text: Audit includes SPSTT; excludes no trust from audit; court leaves request for independent legal status to competent factual determination. Retained HTML is a legal mirror of the court text, not a court-hosted original. Publisher headnote is excluded from claim reasoning. Assertions in quoted committee and trust submissions remain attributed; no audit completion or recovery is inferred. Mirror-only 2021 assertions and edges retain reported tier; the directly retrieved 2020 court judgment remains documented.

documents.title: ADB 51137-003 official project page: finance and contract table
documents.text: Exact L&T package 3 award US$60,232,129.73; loan utilisation reported as of 3 August 2026; AIIB cofinancing separately listed. Live HTML returned 403; original failure body retained. This source is the opened full indexed page, not original live bytes. Signed loan and borrower monitoring PDFs were obtained directly. Contract table says 10 May 2021; borrower monitoring report says signed 9 May 2021. Keep one-day discrepancy explicit. Different sections have different dates. Do not treat older narrative text as a 2026 status update. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/adb-bangladesh-project-indexed.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Loan 3853-BAN: Dhaka and Western Zone loan agreement
documents.text: Bangladesh is sovereign borrower of EUR 271,838,000; it must relend proceeds to PGCB through a subsidiary financing agreement. The US$300 m figure on the project page is an equivalent, not the signed euro principal. Original 2024 closing date was later extended. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/adb-loan-2019.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Dhaka and Western Zone environmental monitoring January–June 2025, Part A
documents.text: Borrower report records package 3 L&T contract 9 May 2021, approximately 85% progress by June 2025, rejected monitoring submission and planned corrective action. Borrower/consultant monitoring report, not a judicial finding or independent completion certificate. Front cover month August 2025; report version 20 August 2025. Package 8 termination is a different contractor/package and is not attributed to L&T. No later completion certification verified. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/adb-monitoring-2025.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: PMGKY P173943/P174027 joint implementation completion report
documents.text: P174027 approved 15 December 2020; closed 31 December 2022. IDA 68130 actual US$111,201,860 and 68120 actual US$291,400,000; total US$402,601,860. Cover transposes first-operation IDA/IBRD instrument labels; use correctly identified financing table for P174027, corroborated by original programme document. USD reporting equivalents of SDR credit vary with exchange rates; actual USD 402.60 m vs approved USD 400 m is not evidence of unauthorised overspending. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/ida-pmgky-icr.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: P174027: second COVID social-protection development-policy financing document
documents.text: Proposed SDR 77 m concessional plus US$291.4 m non-concessional IDA credit; proceeds go to GoI RBI account and Consolidated Fund for general budget use. This document is a proposal at publication; final approval/actual financing is established by the completion report. It explicitly says proceeds do not finance specifically agreed activities. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/ida-pmgky-pd.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: IFC participates in Bajaj Finance US$1 bn fund raise
documents.text: IFC identifies its own US$400 m loan within larger US$1 bn fundraising and anticipated climate/microfinance objectives. US$600 m mobilisation from other lenders is not IFC own-account cash. Targets for 2027 are not realised outcomes. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/ifc-bajaj-announcement.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: IFC project 50037: BFL Loan FY 25
documents.text: Senior secured loan up to US$400 m to Bajaj Finance; US$100 m microfinance and up to US$300 m climate use; approved 9 August, signed 30 August, invested 9 September 2024. Invested status is not a published drawdown ledger; up-to ceilings and intended on-lending do not identify ultimate customers. Last updated 17 October 2024. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/ifc-bajaj-project.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: IFC project 42622: Mahindra LMM Co
documents.text: Names Mahindra Last Mile Mobility Limited; equity/compulsorily convertible instrument, not sovereign lending; investment event 3 October 2023. Last updated 8 October 2023. IFC investment event differs from issuer allotment 9 October 2023; these are different recorded milestones, not silently merged. Expected benefits are projections. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/ifc-mahindra-project.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: India 2025 Article IV report: informational annex
documents.text: Earlier official snapshot independently records no outstanding purchases or loans; Article IV consultation is surveillance, not a lending approval. Data date 30 September 2025 differs from report publication and 2026 financial position. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/imf-articleiv-2025-original.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: India: Financial Position in the Fund,30 September 2026
documents.text: Outstanding purchases and loans: None; quota, reserve tranche, SDR allocation/holdings and projected charges shown separately. This is a dated financial position; it does not prove an absence of every IMF-related financial obligation. IMF notes table is informational and does not replace other official statements. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/imf-position-2026.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: India: Transactions with the Fund through 30 September 2026
documents.text: No purchase/loan transaction rows in 2011–2026; corroborates the dated no-outstanding-credit snapshot. No transaction rows is not a universal no-influence claim. This table excludes quota/SDR transactions and does not imply zero SDR charges. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/imf-transactions-2026.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Mahindra exchange filing: MLMML cash allotment to IFC
documents.text: 30,00,000 CCPS at ₹1,000 each allotted for ₹300 cr cash; 5.9% voting-instruction rights until conversion, within an up-to ₹600 cr commitment. Issuer filing and receipt statement, not an independently obtained bank ledger. Later tranches/conversion are not verified. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/mahindra-cash-2023.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: General Allocation of Special Drawing Rights by the IMF
documents.text: India received SDR 12.57 bn allocation effective 23 August 2021; total holdings became SDR 13.66 bn; RBI says holdings form part of foreign exchange reserves. Allocation, total holdings and USD equivalents are different quantities. This is not a sovereign project loan or a fiscal grant. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/rbi-sdr-release.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: World Bank procurement notices P150395: OP00218737 and OP00187128
documents.text: WRD purchaser, loan 84880-IN linkage, two named awarded bidders, one signed contract price and comparator bids. 13 March 2023 is award-notification date, not a verified signature date. The notice establishes no legal JV name, per-firm share or cash payment. The complete 115-notice response contains unrelated packages. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/tn-awards.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: TNSUDP P150395 implementation completion report
documents.text: IBRD actual disbursement US$352,729,993 and programme closure 31 March 2023; satisfactory overall outcome coexists with procurement and safeguard concerns. Programme totals and findings cannot be assigned to the selected flood-monitoring contract without contract-specific evidence. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/tn-completion.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: 8488-IN amendment: removal of credit enhancement facility
documents.text: Removes credit enhancement component and reallocates categories; US$400 m aggregate unchanged in this amendment. Amendment effective on last required countersignature and receipt, not automatically the covering-letter date. Later ICR records further changes. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/tn-loan-amendment.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Loan 8488-IN: signed India–IBRD loan agreement
documents.text: US$400 m loan to India; Union makes proceeds available to Tamil Nadu, which makes proceeds available to TNUDF and eligible bodies. Signed historical terms, not a current debt balance. Date corroborated by original 2020 amendment because scanned handwriting is poorly extracted. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/tn-loan-original.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: 8488-IN: TNUDF–TNUIFSL Project Agreement
documents.text: Exact implementing entities and Part B duties; projected net revenue must cover debt service before additional debt. TNUDF is a fund; TNUIFSL is a separate company. Neither is automatically the purchaser of every project contract. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/international-finance-evidence/tn-project-tnudf.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: ADB completion report: Uttarakhand Emergency Assistance Project, January 2021
documents.text: Names Government of India as borrower and Uttarakhand SDMA as executing agency; reports $168.34m actual ADB financing and highly successful completion rating. ADB’s lender assessment concerns its UEAP project; it is not a CAG paragraph-settlement report and does not establish recovery of particular advances. Direct original returned HTTP 403; official-origin indexed text was opened and archived. Publication known to month only.

documents.title: Bihar CAG Report 5 of 2022, Chapter II: PM-KISAN
documents.text: Records validation-detected ineligible payment cohorts, ₹62.67cr recoverable estimate and Secretary’s February 2022 statement of ₹5cr recovered, pending reconciliation/remittance. Official-origin text read through Exa indexed extraction. Direct CAG PDF fetch returned HTTP 503; this is not a successful original download. Indexed extraction and failed access receipts are archived separately. An audit finding is attributed to CAG; it is not a judicial finding of criminal liability. Audit scope FY2018–19–FY2020–21; selected statewide validation/recovery figures updated to November 2021/February 2022. The database-access limitation and sampled field checks are disclosed separately.

documents.title: Government reply: ineligible PM-KISAN beneficiaries and recovery
documents.text: States that ₹416cr had been recovered nationally and land seeding, Aadhaar-based payment and eKYC became mandatory progressively from instalments 12–15. A national ministry-reported recovery aggregate, not a reconciliation of the Bihar audit cohorts. Original HTML directly retrieved with HTTP 200 and retained; government figures are not independently re-audited here.

documents.title: Telangana State Finances Audit Report, year ended March 2022, Report 2 of 2023
documents.text: Names Vijaya Bank (now Bank of Baroda), DGP and TSPHCL; separates ₹500cr borrowing, ₹328cr budget-backed debt service, ₹185cr principal, ₹143cr interest and ₹13cr estimated extra interest. Official-origin text read through Exa indexed extraction. Direct CAG PDF fetch returned HTTP 503; this is not a successful original download. Indexed extraction and failed access receipts are archived separately. An audit finding is attributed to CAG; it is not a judicial finding of criminal liability. Indexed extraction capped at 300,000 characters; the complete relevant Box 2.4 and notes were retained, not the entire original report. No later account-specific repayment or CAG/PAC settlement was retrieved.

documents.title: Telangana Police Housing Corporation: memorandum of association
documents.text: The corporation’s own public objects authorise borrowing and government arrangements, providing a lawful institutional explanation for the financing structure. Undated current company webpage; not the 2018 loan agreement or evidence of compliance with the loan’s repayment clause. Original HTML directly retrieved with HTTP 200 and retained.

documents.title: CAG Report 2 of 2018: reconstruction after Uttarakhand’s 2013 disaster
documents.text: Identifies project funding, state releases versus lender reimbursements, two advance-payment cohorts and utilisation-certificate observations; includes February/March 2018 departmental replies. Official-origin text read through Exa indexed extraction. Direct CAG PDF fetch returned HTTP 503; this is not a successful original download. Indexed extraction and failed access receipts are archived separately. An audit finding is attributed to CAG; it is not a judicial finding of criminal liability. Report numbered 2018, tabled 22 February 2019; the audit financial position is principally March 2018.

documents.title: CAG publication record: Uttarakhand reconstruction audit
documents.text: Establishes that Report 2 of 2018 was tabled 22 February 2019. Publication record read through indexed extraction; not an action-taken outcome.

documents.title: Rajya Sabha answer on six-airport PPP design
documents.text: No prior airport experience, no cap on airports bid, per-passenger fee rather than revenue share; 50 year concessions awarded 2020–21. Official retrospective policy explanation, not the signed 2018 PPPAC minutes or airport-specific payment ledger. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/airports-policy.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Effective date of Bamnipal and Tata Steel BSL amalgamation into Tata Steel
documents.text: Reports NCLT-sanctioned amalgamation became effective 11 November 2021. Historical ownership entities cease to be shown as currently separate operating subsidiaries solely on the 2018 acquisition. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/bhushan-merger-2021.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Neeraj Singal & another v Tata Steel, CA(AT)(Ins)988/2021
documents.text: SBI initiated CIRP; 2018 approval implemented; 2021 SC appeal withdrawn; NCLAT dismissed promoter-share appeal requiring sale at ₹2 per share. This is Bhushan Steel/Tata Steel BSL, not Bhushan Power & Steel/JSW. It does not decide all criminal or tax matters of former promoters. Latest independently read disposition of this specific share dispute is 7 March 2022. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/bhushan-share-order-2022.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Association for Democratic Reforms v Union of India, 2024 INSC 113
documents.text: Constitution Bench struck down electoral-bond anonymity and unlimited corporate funding; ordered issuance stopped and SBI disclosures. This judgment does not establish that any particular donation purchased a government favour; later implementation deadlines are separate. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/bonds-judgment-2024.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act 2015, Act 11
documents.text: Auction/allotment, vesting and statutory tribunal framework for cancelled-block reallocations. Deemed commencement 21 October 2014; not a complete current consolidation. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/coal-act-2015.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Allocation of coal blocks, tranche-wise
documents.text: Official table records Odisha, Vedanta Ltd, auction/sale-of-coal, allocation 3 March 2021 and 6 MTPA. Historical May 2023-hosted allocation snapshot; no production or state cash receipts established. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/coal-allocations-2023.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Notice declaring successful bidders, CMSP 11th/MMDR 1st tranche
documents.text: Radhikapur West auction 2 November 2020 won by Vedanta Limited/bidder 68522 at 21% revenue share. PDF has no printed publication date. Auction date, declaration date and agreement date are distinct. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/coal-auction-winners-2020.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Commercial coal auction methodology:2020 order and 2021/2022/2025 amendments
documents.text: Final 2020 methodology uses revenue-share bids payable to states, 4% floor and unrestricted sale/utilisation; later underground-only concessions are separately dated. Do not use January 2020 discussion-paper terms; 2025 underground 2% floor/upfront waiver applies prospectively to specified future tranches, not automatically to Radhikapur. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/coal-methodology-2025-annex 2020.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020 launch
documents.text: Government states DAP 2020 applicable 1 October 2020 and compares indigenous-content thresholds. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/dap-commencement.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020 (retained official 11 November 2021 version)
documents.text: Indian-IDDM 50% indigenous content and no offsets in ab-initio single-vendor cases including IGA/FMS. Retained 691 page official version includes updates; not every 2021 clause is asserted as present at original launch. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/defence-dap-2020.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Noel Harper v Union of India, WPC 566/2021 and connected matters
documents.text: Court records 2020 FCRA changes and upholds sections 7,12(1A),12A,17, reading down identification to permit Indian passport. Section 8 administrative-expense change is reproduced as legislative context; conclusion expressly lists the challenged provisions. No NGO-specific diversion or adverse finding follows from foreign funding. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/fcra-judgment-2022.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Finance Act 2017, Act 7 of 2017
documents.text: Section 154 removed Companies Act 182 profit cap and party-specific company disclosure; associated provisions enabled electoral bonds. Historical enacted version; specified electoral-funding provisions were struck down in February 2024. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/finance-act-2017-court.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Electricity Green Energy Open Access Rules 2022, GSR 418(E)
documents.text: 100 kW entry threshold, 15 day access decision, green procurement and banking/charge framework. Historical rules were later challenged and struck down by Karnataka HC; do not present this text as an uncontested nationwide current entitlement. Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/green-open-access-2022.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.title: Corporate insolvency resolutions as at 30 September 2022
documents.text: Named debtor CINs, admitted financial/operational claims and realizable amounts under approved plans. Data supplied by resolution professionals. Amounts are realizable, not NPV and not verified cash recovery. 2022 snapshot cannot settle subsequent implementation, appeals or guarantee recoveries. Reused original research/raw/investigation/evidence/finance/ibbi-resolutions.pdf, page 2 row 25; hashes in reused-evidence-manifest.json.

documents.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, Act 31
documents.text: Creditor-initiated corporate resolution, creditor voting and binding adjudicated plans. Original enactment is historical, not a consolidated 2026 statement. Commencement was provision-specific under section 1(3). Archive: research/raw/atlas-expansion/policy-evidence/ibc-original-2016.receipt.json; original bytes and extracted text are distinct artifacts.

documents.text: Resolution-applicant disqualifications and connected-person test, with specified cure/exception provisions. documents.title: CAG Karnataka Report No. 12 of 2025: implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission
documents.text: Section 3.3.1 records incomplete work in Hebbal, Shirahatti taluk, Gadag district during 2024 despite Har Ghar Jal reported status. Government responded in May 2025 that the elevated reservoir was completed by 8 April 2025, with 200 m pipeline and 20 FHTCs remaining before certification/trial run. Section 3.5 discusses 33 tenders worth ₹251.75 crore invited/awarded after 31 March 2024; Government cites timely administrative approvals and delays from non-participation and re-tendering. Sections 3.7.1–3.7.2 identify missing cross-system project/contractor keys and 9,342 first-call single-bid awards among 38,231 finalised works, with government response. Report sample is 28 villages in seven districts; it is not a statewide failure rate. Har Ghar Jal reported status and certified status differ. Audit period begins before requested window; Hebbal implementation findings from 2024 and response from 2025 are separately dated. No evidence of current 2026 conditions or individual guilt is inferred. Exact original publication day unconfirmed; direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 503. Section 3.5 distinguishes extended award deadlines: 15 March 2024 for in-village works and 31 March 2024 for multi-village schemes. The 33 flagged tenders were after the later date; no universal 31 March deadline is inferred. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/services-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.text: Paragraph 3.3.4 attributes ₹46.27 crore paid for overlapping manpower/PMA work. documents.title: The Akshaya Patra Foundation Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Contains audited trust financial statements signed 7 October 2025, programme narrative, a Chikkajala kitchen table and note 2.25 related-party disclosures. documents.title: GLAS Trust Company LLC v BYJU Raveendran: 2024 INSC 811
documents.text: Primary judgment separates the US credit facility, Indian guarantee, settlement objections and the statutory insolvency-withdrawal procedure. ₹158 crore was ordered held by the committee of creditors in escrow. Paragraphs 86–87 expressly decline merits adjudication and any finding on stakeholder conduct. Recited allegations about US transfers are not treated as findings of this Indian judgment.

documents.text: Reports that the trial court heard the discharge pleas following a High Court direction and again refused discharge. Original discharge and remand orders not retrieved. documents.text: Records the clinical defence, State allegations and expert-review material considered at bail. Later bail developments are separately retained. Patient names are not entities in the structured slice.

documents.title: Khyati supplementary charge sheet names hospital holding company

documents.text: Supreme Court allowed the petition and directed release on bail after noting bail granted to the co-accused. This supersedes the earlier custody snapshot. documents.title: CAG Report 10 of 2023: NSAP publicity expenditure
documents.text: Traces approved publicity heads, work orders to DAVP, actual NSAP IEC charge and lack of work-execution confirmation. Direct original PDF again returned HTTP 503 on 7 October 2026. documents.title: Lok Sabha Standing Committee 31 st report: NSAP action taken
documents.text: Checked later parliamentary scrutiny of NSAP. The report concerns scheme recommendations and does not establish settlement of CAG §5.5.1’s 2017 DAVP transactions. Non-observation in this document does not prove no remediation happened elsewhere.

documents.title: Rajya Sabha reply: measures to prevent misuse of AB-PMJAY
documents.text: Documents the ministry’s national anti-fraud and audit mechanism; not a Khyati-specific recovery order. National disciplinary totals cannot be attributed to a named hospital without a hospital-specific order.

documents.title: AISHE Report 2023-24
documents.text: 48,246 colleges were registered and 46,468 responded. Of responding colleges, 17.1% were government, 12.9% private aided and 70.0% private unaided. Contains state tables for private/government colleges and district distribution. Responding-college percentages must not be applied as exact counts to all registered colleges. Institution prevalence is not a funding share.

documents.title: Union Ministry releases AISHE 2022-23 and 2023-24 reports
documents.text: For 2023-24, 59,533 of 64,756 registered HEIs participated. Higher education enrolment is reported as 4.50 crore in 2023-24. GER is 30 in 2023-24 and uses ages 18-23 population projections based on Census 2011. Participation is voluntary and data is self-reported by institutions. Registration, survey response and estimated enrolment have different denominators. Report reference period differs from publication date.

documents.title: AISHE Final Reports
documents.text: Lists 2023-24 and 2022-23 final reports and Excel files. Index page is a discovery source, not a transaction or district funding ledger.

documents.title: Akshaya Patra Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Foundation describes PM POSHAN implementation for government/government-aided schools. Report says FY 2024–25 operations cover 16 states and 3 UTs. Government contributions are reported as ₹42,093.64 lakh and total income ₹85,746.61 lakh. New kitchens include Bengaluru locations, Pilerne in Goa and Kanpur. Government contributions include Anganwadi nutrition; not all school funding. Government contribution is within total income; avoid double counting. Kitchen city coverage is not equivalent to school-recipient district or a grant amount. States/cities arrays are documented examples, not full footprint.

documents.title: Azim Premji University Bengaluru Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Report identifies the university as not-for-profit, private and established under a Karnataka Act. Azim Premji Foundation is named sponsoring body. Report provides institutional teaching and research context. No university donation or scholarship amount validated in this extraction. Private university status does not imply eligibility for private equity distribution. Do not generalize one institution's funding arrangements to all private colleges.

documents.title: Five years, 10 states: Where India's government school count fell the most
documents.text: Reports uneven state-level net school-count reductions and warns against reading stock differences as a simple linear demographic story. Secondary lead, not proof of individual closures or wrongdoing. Do not import the headline as a closure-event count.

documents.title: Educate Girls FCRA financial statements for year ended 31 March 2024
documents.text: Document is financial statements prepared under FCRA for foreign contribution received and utilised. Income statement reports ₹1,08,44,95,261 donations for year ended 31 March 2024, separately from other income. Statements are signed 16 December 2024. PDF table extraction is fragmented; manually verify layout before treating each expense line as structured. Organisation-wide foreign donations do not establish donor-by-city or school-level funding. Upload path 2026 is not the fiscal year or signature date.

documents.title: Educate Girls Annual Progress Report FY 2024–25
documents.text: Audacious Project narrative identifies Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar expansion geography. FY 2024–25 report self-reports 285,237 girls enrolled through Vidya. Report describes two temporary learning centres in Prayagraj during Maha Kumbh for migrant workers' children. Programme outcomes are organisation-reported. No city-level monetary allocation established. The four named states describe a particular initiative, not necessarily the full NGO footprint. Annual programme reach cannot be summed with individual-school enrolment without deduplication.

documents.title: FCRA Online Services dashboard
documents.text: Dashboard distinguishes active/alive association count from annual returns filed across active, expired, cancelled and deemed ceased associations. State breakdown is explicitly for all association types. Registry counts are not education NGO counts or funding amounts. Snapshot may lag and uses legacy place names. Association address is not beneficiary location; do not map receipts to headquarters as local school funding.

documents.title: FCRA Online Services: Annual Returns (FC-4)
documents.text: Official portal provides FC-4 annual return filing guidance, sample form and document requirements. Portal landing page proves reporting route, not receipt by a particular school. FCRA registration or prior permission is not evidence of donation receipt or programme deployment. Sample-form fetch returned no extracted page content.

documents.title: HDFC Bank Parivartan CSR Report FY 2024–25
documents.text: CSR education work includes remedial learning, teacher training, scholarships and safe school infrastructure. ECSS supports continuation of education for economically vulnerable students. Projects implemented directly or through empanelled partners; disclosures also appear in directors' report and MCA filings. ₹1,068.03 crore report total covers all CSR sectors, not education alone; exclude from education totals. Report reach across 28 states/8 UTs refers to overall CSR, not proof of education spend in every jurisdiction. Current open scholarship applications or eligibility deadlines not verified here.

documents.title: 100 schools with zero enrolment denotified, 120 merged
documents.text: Reports 100 zero-enrolment primary/middle schools denotified and 120 primary schools with five or fewer students merged. Reports difficult-terrain and tribal-area schools were exempted from merger. Original school-wise notifications not obtained. Counts refer to different administrative actions and should remain separate. Zero enrolment and low enrolment are the official rationale reported; no matched catchment population evidence establishes a contradiction.

documents.title: Government urged to withdraw order allowing merger of low-enrolment schools
documents.text: Reports minister's statement that government has no plans to shut any government school. Reports AIDSO seeking withdrawal of a merger clause and a written assurance. Capture minister's denial alongside access concerns. School closure, transfer of classes and administrative merger may refer to different units. No inference of dishonesty or wrongdoing.

documents.title: Karnataka rolls out project to merge government schools with KPS magnet schools
documents.text: Reports a seven-school pilot linked to Honganuru KPS. Quotes circular instructions on student transfers and transport arrangements. Reports concern from educationists/student organisations about rural access. Underlying circular not retrieved in this pass. Announced/proposed state scale is not completed implementation. Allegation that a much larger number of schools would close is not adopted as a fact.

documents.title: KKR and PSP invest in Lighthouse Learning
documents.text: KKR funds invest alongside new investor PSP; KKR continues to hold a majority stake. Recipient described as an education services provider/platform. Release names presence in Bangalore, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad and Delhi-NCR. No transaction amount disclosed in the primary announcement. Do not substitute media transaction estimates as primary-verified values. Equity in services platform is distinct from donations to schools, ownership of regulated educational trusts, or FCRA contributions. Presence is not proof investment proceeds were spent in every named city; Delhi NCR crosses administrative borders. Delhi-NCR presence is a regional label; it does not establish a school or spending location within Delhi's administrative boundary.

documents.title: Closure of Government Schools — Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 1374
documents.text: Annexure I reports government-school stock counts for five academic years by state/UT. Annexure II reports government-school stock counts for all Uttar Pradesh districts. India government schools: 1,022,386 in 2021-22 and 1,005,245 in 2025-26. NEP paragraph 7.4 says consolidation should only proceed when access is unaffected. The answer provides stock counts, not a school-by-school closure or merger register. Districts are not cities or school catchments. No matched population series or causal impact evaluation is provided. Reported by states/UTs through UDISE+.

documents.title: Declining Enrolment of Students in Government Schools in Uttar Pradesh — Lok Sabha Question 2445
documents.text: Provides approved central and actual released central shares for Uttar Pradesh Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI for three financial years. Shamli district government-school counts rise from 621 in 2021-22 to 623 in 2025-26. The requested district spending is answered with state-level approved/released figures; do not label these district spending. Releases are not expenditure, audited utilisation, or money received by an individual school. Annexures contain government-school counts, not verified closure events.

documents.title: National CSR Portal: company-wise project disclosures
documents.text: Schema includes project, sector, state, district, amount outlay in INR crore, amount spent in INR crore and implementation mode. Captcha and dynamic selection prevent treating landing page as a project extract. Company registered office must not be substituted for project location. documents.text: Portal provides year, state, PSU/non-PSU and development sector filters and an implementing agency master. Heading and filter years differ; verify downloaded report timestamp before publishing totals.

documents.title: Cabinet approves MERITE with ₹4,200 crore outlay
documents.text: Scheme targets 175 engineering institutions and 100 polytechnics. Total financial implication is ₹4,200 crore, including ₹2,100 crore World Bank loan assistance. documents.text: Total project cost ₹27,360 crore, including central share ₹18,128 crore, over five years. Targets more than 14,500 existing schools managed by central/state/UT/local government. Not a grant programme for all private unaided schools. National targets do not verify city-level awards.

documents.text: At the page's update, 12,079 schools had been selected through four phases. Confirms ₹27,360 crore total and ₹18,128 crore central project cost. Selection snapshot is dated November 2024 and must not be labelled current in October 2026.

documents.title: PM-USHA: Building Stronger Institutions for a Knowledge-Driven Future
documents.text: Scheme outlay ₹12,926.10 crore for 2023-24 to 2025-26. First two PAB meetings approved 440 units worth ₹5,613.12 crore. FY 2025-26 budget stated as ₹1,815 crore. Eight new model degree college units approved across Nagaland (4), Manipur (2), Meghalaya (2), totaling ₹119.98 crore. Outlay, PAB approvals and annual budget are distinct stages and cannot be added together. A unit is not necessarily a unique institution. Snapshot is May 2025; not live allocations.

documents.title: PM-USHA Guidelines
documents.text: Covers government and government-aided higher education institutions of states/UTs. Gives priority to focus districts and defines components and eligibility. Eligibility and programme scope do not establish that an institution has received funding. Historical AISHE figures in the guidelines are not current counts.

documents.title: Population Projections for India and States 2011–2036
documents.text: Uses Census 2011, SRS fertility/mortality and migration assumptions. Projects total population increase and a decline in the national population aged 5–14 during 2011–2036. Projections are model-based rather than new census observations. Total population growth cannot substitute for school-age population growth. District/city downscaling requires separate validation. Mirrored copies surfaced differing summary totals; numeric population claims are intentionally omitted until document edition provenance is reconciled.

documents.title: Pratham Education Foundation Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Report describes direct learning programmes and district, city and state government partnerships. Report contains financials and supporters sections. Historical Mumbai narrative does not prove current city funding allocation. No financial totals from this report validated; full financial section not extracted in this pass.

documents.title: Quota for EWS Seats in Private Unaided Schools — Lok Sabha Question 1260
documents.text: Provides sanctioned and reimbursed-to-school amounts under RTE for Karnataka for five years. FY 2025-26 sanctioned ₹156.10 crore and reimbursed ₹148.68 crore. Government says reimbursement is timely, based on information from the state. Describes 2018 Karnataka neighbourhood-school exemption. Including Bengaluru does not make this city-level funding. The table covers the reimbursement claim population; do not interpret as uniquely new entry-grade admissions without checking definitions. Sanctioned less reimbursed does not establish overdue obligations or misuse. Distinct from central releases to the state; do not sum with Samagra central share as independent money.

documents.title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
documents.text: Section 12(1)(c) provides entry-level admissions for eligible disadvantaged/weaker-section children of at least 25% in specified categories of schools. Section 12(2) provides private unaided school reimbursement capped at state per-child expenditure or actual charge, whichever is lower, with provisos for pre-existing free-education obligations. Not an unrestricted private-school capital grant. School eligibility, constitutional/applicability exclusions, neighbourhood rules and claims are determined by applicable law and state implementation. Statutory eligibility is not evidence of payment.

documents.title: Chhattisgarh Samagra Shiksha 2025-26 revised PAB minutes
documents.text: Approved annual work plan: ₹232,029.17 lakh including ₹82,492.13 lakh spillover. Planned central share to be released: ₹112,900.28 lakh; corresponding state share ₹75,267.52 lakh. documents.text: Provides state/UT financial-year entries with minutes, supplementary minutes, addenda and revisions. An index to retrieve further records, not extracted transaction coverage. documents.title: Tata Trusts Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Grant disbursal table reports ₹247.47 crore education institutional/direct implementation spend and ₹40.91 crore education individual grants. documents.text: Reports 104,125 single-teacher schools and 7,993 zero-enrolment schools in 2024-25. Reports total teachers 10,122,420. documents.title: Report on UDISE+ 2023-24 — existing structure
documents.text: Separates government, government-aided, private unaided recognised, and other schools. Reports that student-wise collection from 2022-23 is not strictly comparable with earlier aggregate reporting for several education indicators. documents.title: UP govt tells HC: No merger if school has over 50 students, 1km distance
documents.text: Reports extension of interim status quo for school pairing in Sitapur until 1 September 2025. Reports government assurances on enrolment/distance and court clarification that interim order does not affect overall policy. Historical interim procedural status, not current case disposition. Later court orders must be obtained before stating present legality or operative stay.

documents.title: Krishna Kumari and others v State of UP — 2025:AHC-LKO:38113
documents.text: Paragraph 3 identifies Government Order 16 June 2025 and consequent 24 June 2025 list of 105 schools challenged in petitions. documents.title: No merger for schools with 50 or more students as Uttar Pradesh government revises plan
documents.text: Reports minister's clarification excluding schools with 50 or more students and schools farther than 1km from pairing. Reports minister saying UDISE codes remain unchanged, buildings may host Bal Vatikas, and original classes can resume if enrolment/capacity warrants. Reported policy and explanation, not independent verification of implementation. Do not turn nearly 10,000 proposed pairings into confirmed permanent closures. Preserved codes mean stock series can miss changes in where teaching takes place.

documents.title: World Bank approves STARS to improve India's education system
documents.text: World Bank approved a USD 500 million STARS programme. Programme supports quality and governance of school education in six named states. Loan maturity 17.5 years including five-year grace period. Approval is not disbursement or per-state allocation. Source page extraction metadata says 2021-01-29 but article dateline is June 24, 2020; use dateline. Countrywide beneficiaries and six-state activities must not be treated as identical scope.

documents.title: STARS implementation status and results report, ISR59758
documents.text: Report states cumulative disbursement of USD 196.75 million (39.35%) against the USD 500 million programme. Report discusses programme restructuring and a requested extension. documents.title: Adani Power annual report FY2022-23, filed 27 June 2023
documents.text: Reports Essar Power MP acquisition/control on 16 March 2022, rename to Mahan Energen, ₹1 crore equity infusion and ₹600 crore upfront lender payment; locates 1,200MW plant in Singrauli. documents.title: IBBI summary of Supreme Court Essar Steel judgment

documents.text: 1,484 resolution plans; ₹435,469.89 crore creditor realization measure against ₹1,426,665.38 crore admitted claims; methodology and fair-value denominator caveats. documents.text: Named debtor CINs, admitted financial/operational claims and realizable amounts under approved plans. Data supplied by resolution professionals. documents.text: Current original page links audited FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 accounts; both were downloaded. Comparator supplies context, not a causal or intent test.

documents.text: Defines compromise and technical write-off separately; board governance, criminal-proceedings preservation and continued penal measures for wilful default/fraud. documents.title: SEBI final order: Adicorp transactions — 31671/2025-26
documents.text: SEBI found the specified show-cause allegations unestablished under the rules applicable to the transactions and disposed of proceedings without directions. A final regulatory decision on specified noticees/transactions, not a criminal acquittal or clearance of every allegation involving a corporate group. Original cover identities reviewed; personal tax identifiers excluded from the retained excerpts.

documents.title: Parliament reply: proceedings based on CAG findings — Lok Sabha Q.2191
documents.text: The Ministry reports CBI RC33/2022-EO-III-Delhi, registered 12 July 2022 on a coal-allocation audit, with a closure report filed 31 March 2025; it describes ATN/PAC follow-up. The underlying case file and closure order were not retrieved.

This constitutional decision does not adjudicate whether an individual donation bought an award. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.text: The Court declined an omnibus SIT under Article 32 where ordinary remedies had not been pursued. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.text: The Court considered the PMLA arrest challenge, referred questions about necessity of arrest, and granted interim bail. Paragraph 88 expressly reserves criminal merits. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

A final regulatory decision on specified noticees/transactions, not a criminal acquittal or clearance of every allegation involving a corporate group. documents.text: Historical judgment refuses compulsory transfer of PM CARES funds to NDRF and distinguishes their legal/audit regimes. Does not establish current financial balances, donor identities, procurement delivery or general RTI status.

documents.text: SBI sought time until 30 June 2024. The Court required disclosure by 12 March and ECI publication by 15 March; contempt jurisdiction was not exercised at that stage.
