documents.text: The seven-judge bench held legislative speech/vote immunity does not immunise bribery prosecution. The reference answers the constitutional question, not individual criminal guilt. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.title: SWAMIH / Gayatri Aura information dispute — Delhi HC W.P.(C) 4353/2025
documents.text: The Court declined the RTI petition on forum/territorial grounds with liberty to approach the jurisdictional High Court; all rights and contentions remain open. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.title: Vishal Tiwari v Union of India — 2024 INSC 3
documents.text: No ground was shown to transfer SEBI investigations; the Court directed completion of two pending matters and expressly did not interfere with investigation outcomes. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.title: CPPP historical award scrape — retained aggregate analysis
documents.text: Buyer-level historical bid-count aggregates, explicit deduplication and data-quality defects. New sector lenses classify public-body labels; they do not re-read raw tender rows. Historical scrape of unknown completeness. All 40 sampled stored portal URLs had expired; row-level agreement with government records remains unknown. No figure is a national procurement statistic. Supplier names are not CINs, contracts, assets or identity-resolved political links. Underlying republisher labels CC-BY-4.0; it did not publish its scraper and cannot establish completeness or government endorsement.

documents.title: Central Public Procurement Portal — tender and award discovery
documents.text: Search official procurement notices and results, then retrieve original notices, corrigenda, award orders and contract documents for an exact procurement process. A discovery link is not proof that a particular tender was downloaded or verified. Portal coverage excludes many purchases on other systems.

documents.title: IRB annual report FY2023-24 — ownership and scope-separated donations
documents.text: Audited consolidated Note 46 reports INR676.20 million political donations: INR360m unspecified electoral bonds, INR300m Bharatiya Janta Party and INR16.20m Balasahebanchi Shivsena. The standalone parent reports NIL political donations. Subsidiary table reports 100% ownership of Modern Road Makers and IRB MP Expressway. Chairman DIN is separately identified. Consolidated amounts belong to the reporting perimeter, not necessarily the listed legal parent or a named subsidiary. The parties behind the INR360m bond component are not identified by this note; no recipient allocation is inferred. These are disclosed relationships; the document establishes no contract influence or misconduct.

documents.title: IRB MP Expressway Private Limited audited financial statements FY2023-24
documents.text: Other expenses include donations INR250 million. The viewed note labels these donations without naming a political recipient or identifying an instrument. Donation is not automatically political contribution. No party edge is created from this row. A secondary electoral-bond matching website was found but the original ECI serial-number files were not retrieved and joined in this work. A shared amount is not an identity or transaction key.

documents.title: Modern Road Makers Private Limited audited financial statements FY2023-24
documents.text: The company reports total donations INR358.62 million, including political-party donations INR350 million. The note does not name recipient parties. This subsidiary note cannot allocate its INR350m to the BJP, Balasahebanchi Shivsena, BRS or any party. Do not add subsidiary donations to the consolidated total: consolidation may already include them. OCR contains a prior-year digit error; the image says March31,2023, and is authoritative.

documents.title: NHAI Delhi–Mumbai Expressway package progress, March2023
documents.text: Official package table names M/s IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd. as concessionaire for Gujarat Package7; award31July2020, commencement10December2021, targetcompletion30June2024, physicalprogress28% at31March2023. This is a historical status snapshot; target completion is not evidence of completion. Package length is rounded28km in the source; chainage interval27.5km is not an independent discrepancy finding. This source contains no political funding or award influence finding.

documents.title: Official Union Council portfolio roster — snapshot as on25July2026
documents.text: Official page identifies portfolio holders including Nitin Jairam Gadkari (roads), Manohar Lal (power), C R Patil (JalShakti), Jagat Prakash Nadda (health), Pralhad Joshi (education), Amit Shah (home), RajNath Singh(defence), Narendra Modi(personnel). The publication date and revised roster snapshot differ. Edges record office at the snapshot date only; exact uninterrupted tenure is not reconstructed from this rolling page. Holding a Union portfolio does not establish involvement in a particular award; policing, health, education and recruitment also have state and local authorities.

documents.title: CAG Report 19 of 2023: Bharatmala Phase I
documents.text: Audit questions project prioritisation, appraisal, elevated design justification and execution. Includes MoRTH replies and auditor rejoinders. The ₹18.20 crore/km programme norm and ₹250.77 crore/km sanctioned urban expressway civil cost have different scope; their ratio is not a measured like-for-like overrun. Primary-host indexed text was read; original PDF retrieval returned HTTP503. Layout repetition/truncation limits downstream extraction. Publication day corroborated by contemporaneous report; audit period predates much of the publication window.

documents.title: Bharatmala corridors and state-wise awarded programme snapshot
documents.text: Annexures identify 25 greenfield corridors and state-wise total/awarded lengths and tentative capital costs. National awarded length is 26,418 km; awarded tentative capital cost ₹8,53,264 crore. Tentative capital cost, award and expenditure are separate stages. Not current status or a contractor ledger. State rows are programme allocation geography, not company addresses.

documents.title: NHAI report on Meachi bridge foundation settlement, NH327E
documents.text: At chainage 24+461 on the Galgalia–Bahadurganj section, the bridge under construction experienced about 600 mm pile-foundation settlement; the preliminary inquiry considered constricted river flow and scour. Preliminary causal explanation and temporary personnel suspensions do not establish final liability. Release names GR Infra Projects Highway Ltd and project concessionaire GR Galgalia Bahadurganj Highway Private Limited distinctly; parent ownership is not inferred. No final inquiry report or contractor reply retrieved. Galgalia and Bahadurganj name corridor endpoints; the exact bridge at chainage 24+461 is not assigned to either locality without geolocation.

documents.title: Parliament bridge/tunnel collapse annexure and actions taken
documents.text: Official incident table distinguishes existing permanent/temporary bridges, under-construction bridges and tunnels, fatalities and actions taken. The source window is relative to August 2024, not the dashboard’s 2021-10-06–2026-10-06 window. NH/MoRTH reporting scope does not cover every municipal, rural or private bridge. Different structures and weather conditions require separate reference classes.

documents.title: Infrastructure stability and progress: parliamentary reply
documents.text: Parent release links the bridge/tunnel collapse annexure and explains national highway programme scope. Publication provenance for the annexure; not an independent corroborating incident source.

documents.title: NHAI action after Cherkkala slope-protection collapse
documents.text: NHAI attributes slope collapse to design, protection and drainage deficiencies, announces debarment and a show-cause notice for one year/up to ₹9 crore, and says reconstruction is at concessionaire cost. Show-cause proposed duration/maximum penalty is not a verified final penalty or present-day debarment status. No contractor response or final expert committee report was located in this source set. HAM 15-year maintenance and own-cost reconstruction mean repair does not establish a second public payment.

documents.title: Guidelines on debarment of firms from bidding
documents.text: Guidelines separate ministry/entity debarment from cross-government debarment, require an opportunity to respond and preserve contracts concluded before an order. Debarment scope, commencement, expiry and allied-firm identity must be read from the actual order. A show-cause notice is not interchangeable with a final order.

documents.title: NHAI letter of award: Dwarka Expressway Package 4
documents.text: PIB identifies Larsen and Toubro as contractor for the Basai RoB–NH8/SPR package, 8.76 km, ₹1,047.007 crore, with two-year construction and four-year maintenance periods. Outside the five-year publication window; retained to resolve the historical contracting entity. Award announcement is not payment, completion certification or the total Dwarka project cost.

documents.title: Ministry official disputes Dwarka cost comparison
documents.text: A senior ministry official says elevated urban works are not comparable with the corridor norm and describes competitive bidding and appraisal. Official is unnamed in the article; this is a reported response, not a signed ministry order. The article’s aggregate estimate and per-km estimate do not form a clean internally consistent denominator; not used to calculate savings.

documents.title: NHAI preliminary report on under-construction Kerala VUP slab collapse
documents.text: Deck slab collapsed while concreting on Chengala–Neeleshwaram NH66. NHAI’s preliminary explanation is scaffolding failure; an NIT expert committee was constituted. Headline says no injuries; body records one minor injury and no casualties. Body is retained. This VUP incident is a different asset and mechanism from the 2025 slope collapse on the same corridor. Preliminary cause is not a final inquiry finding. The August 2024 parliamentary annexure lists a Kerala NH66 VUP staging failure at km 72+297 (PDF pp. 13–14) and reports suspensions/penalty; the 2022 release does not give chainage, so this is not automatically merged as the same asset.

documents.title: QCBS clarification for works and non-consultancy services
documents.text: Clarifies that works of any value may use QCBS following Quality Oriented Procurement procedure; NCS above ₹10 crore require QOP procedure while lower-value NCS follow the specified 2021 route. Clarification of 29 October 2021 instructions, not a blanket replacement of lowest-cost selection. Use depends on prescribed approvals/procedure and the actual procurement.

documents.title: CAG West Bengal Report 1 of 2026: bridge maintenance and road renovation
documents.text: Road and bridge audit includes utility coordination failures, delayed reconstruction and failed Jagatpur–Dharampota road renovation with departmental responses. Exact publication/tabling day not verified; not assigned an invented date. Primary-host indexed text was read; original PDF request received403. Repeated OCR/layout blocks do not represent repeated incidents. Test-checked samples are not statewide prevalence or a current engineering safety assessment.

documents.title: Manual for Procurement of Works, updated June 2022
documents.text: Consolidated guidance includes quality-cum-cost selection and debarment procedures; laws and original instructions prevail if inconsistent. Generic central procurement guidance; check authority-specific manuals and governing tender date. Not a new Act, not retroactive proof that an earlier contract violated later guidance.

documents.title: Manual for Procurement of Works, second edition 2025 (final)
documents.text: Final edition incorporates GFR, DFPR 2024 and mediation developments. It mainly guides ministries with limited engineering capacity; major engineering organisations may retain approved frameworks. PublishedAt records verified republication, not original effective date. The official DoE indexed catalogue lists 5 January 2026 release. The March 2025 draft is excluded. Subsequent amendments require separate verification. The manual does not establish improper favour or retroactively rewrite contracts.

documents.title: Cabinet approval of Agnipath recruitment policy
documents.text: Official policy describes four-year engagement, an opportunity for up to 25% of each specific batch to enter the regular cadre, and Seva Nidhi;46,000 is the announced first-year recruitment plan. Announced intake is not actual enrolment; up to 25% is a ceiling rather than a guarantee for any individual. Financial packages and eligibility must be checked against later service-specific notices; this is the 2022 policy record. Government-stated benefits are attributed policy objectives, not independently measured outcomes.

documents.title: CAG Army audit Report 11 of 2024: official press release
documents.text: Official audit summary records ₹44.26 crore wasteful expenditure on underused hired office accommodation and ₹17.43 crore Chennai warehouse rent linked to delayed replacement construction. Primary official summary was read, but the full report with ministry responses was not retrieved in this pass. Audit financial findings are historical and attributed to CAG; they do not establish guilt of a contractor or politician. No operational force weaknesses or sensitive locations are mapped.

documents.title: MoD signs five capital acquisition contracts,1 March 2024
documents.text: Official release names HAL, Larsen & Toubro and BrahMos Aerospace and separately prices five contracts totalling ₹39,125.39 crore; Defence Minister Rajnath Singh was present at the exchange. Signed contract values are not disbursements, deliveries or completion certificates. Two contracts to a vendor may cover different scopes; repeat-vendor counts alone do not show repeat work. Ministerial presence is an official-role connection and does not demonstrate intervention, preferential treatment or ownership. No corporate-group or political-donation joins are inferred from names alone.

documents.title: Consultation on draft Defence Acquisition Procedure 2026
documents.text: Ministry invited comments on a draft which it said would replace DAP 2020 once approved; release explicitly distinguishes revenue DPM 2025 from capital DAP. This source establishes a draft consultation, not enactment; no effective date is inferred. Later finalisation is not established by this source. Do not infer that a rule remained unchanged merely because a later document was not retrieved.

documents.title: DAP 2020 amendments announced 25 April 2022
documents.text: Capital-acquisition amendment summary covers indigenous sourcing, replacement of Integrity Pact Bank Guarantee with other safeguards, viable splitting among technically qualified vendors, and simplified iDEX/Make-II procedures. Official summary rather than the complete consolidated procedure; contract-specific applicability and operative orders must be checked. Splitting an order can be expressly permitted by policy; multiple awards are not automatically evasion.

documents.title: Union Budget 2026-27, Demand 21: Capital Outlay on Defence Services
documents.text: Official capital demand supplies fiscal-stage context for acquisition and construction, separately from revenue/pay and pensions. A budget allocation does not identify an awarded vendor, beneficiary, delivery or payment. Exact publication day not independently verified.

documents.title: Union Budget 2026-27, Demand 20: Defence Services(Revenue)
documents.text: Official revenue demand separates pay/allowances and other service heads including Agnipath, making personnel expenditure distinguishable from capital acquisition. Budget heads are not person-level payment or appointment records. Defence pensions are a separate demand and are not a procurement award. Exact publication day not independently verified.

documents.title: Defence Procurement Manual 2025 release and transition
documents.text: Revenue-procurement manual revises liquidated damages, limited-tender provisions, indigenisation orders and procurement procedures; transition depends on RFP issue/reissue date. Revenue procurement is distinct from capital acquisition under DAP. The reported approximately ₹1 lakhcrore is the procurement scope described by the release, not an awarded contract or spent total. Full manual and contract terms control any finding of breach.

documents.title: Public Examinations Act 2024 consolidated as on 31 July 2026
documents.text: Primary consolidated statute incorporates 2026 amendments to penalties and service-provider debarment plus Special Task Force, fast-track investigation/trial and appeal provisions. 31 July 2026 is the stated legal-version/effective date, not a independently verified web-publication date. Apply provisions to the relevant conduct/date/jurisdiction; the central Schedule is not a blanket statement that every state recruitment examination is covered. The original 2024 penalties are superseded for the amended provisions; prior events must not be reassessed as if later penalties applied then.

documents.title: Public Examinations Act 2024: enactment and enforcement metadata
documents.text: Official statute metadata distinguishes presidential enactment from commencement on 21 June 2024. The live index reflects later amendments; use dated legal versions rather than treating the original 2024 text as unchanged.

documents.title: Public Examinations Rules 2024: published transcription of GSR 342(E)
documents.text: Transcription sets out computer-based-test standards, service-provider reporting, centre coordinator/regional officer responsibilities and monitoring. Secondary transcription read; original Gazette binary was not retrieved in this pass. Capped at reported evidence. The publication date of this webpage is 25 June 2024; rules state commencement on Gazette publication,24 June 2024. No inference that a particular exam contractor breached these rules follows from the rule alone.

documents.title: General Financial Rules 2017 updated to 31 July 2024
documents.text: Rule 149 records GeM thresholds of ₹50,000 and ₹10 lakh following 10 July 2024 amendment, with rate-reasonableness and competition conditions; Rules 154–155 retain separate outside-GeM conditions and scientific-organisation exceptions. Consolidation date is not verified publication day; this is a historical rules snapshot, not a claim of unchanged 2026 rules. Goods, services, works and scientific exceptions must be distinguished; Union GFR is not automatically every state rule. Automobiles have an explicit no-ceiling exception under 149(i); threshold screening must not flag them solely by amount.

documents.title: MHA announces priority for returning Agniveers in CAPFs and Assam Rifles
documents.text: MHA announced priority in CAPF and Assam Rifles recruitment for Agniveers completing four years and said a detailed plan was being prepared. This announcement is not a recruitment-rule notification or actual appointment count. CAPFs/Assam Rifles are distinct from state police, and priority does not establish appointment of any named person.

documents.title: Odisha e-Procurement IT Audit, Report 1 of 2025
documents.text: CAG documents procurement-evaluation and contract-value errors, including a Bargarh boundary-wall award above the price payable under the applicable preference rule; the report records departmental responses. Selected audit cases do not establish the prevalence of irregularity in all Odisha contracts. Historical process findings do not establish the present condition of a live system. Public financial controls are summarised; no system exploitation instructions or private bidder identifiers are reproduced.

documents.title: Union Budget 2026-27, Demand 51: Police
documents.text: Official demand separates Union police and related organisations, revenue/capital and fiscal stages; suitable for tracing allocation categories before seeking actual payments. Union demand does not measure all state-police budgets; Delhi Police is not a proxy for all cities. BE and RE are budget provisions, not awarded contracts or actual expenditure; do not sum stage columns. Exact publication day not independently verified.

documents.title: Telangana State Finances Audit Report, year ended March 2022, Report 2 of 2023
documents.text: CAG traces ₹500 crore police-vehicle borrowing through TSPHCL, ₹328 crore budget-funded repayment by March 2022 and estimated ₹13 crore additional interest; separately examines police grant controls and Safe City budget utilisation. Report year is not a verified publication day; exact publication date remains unknown in this record. Budget, borrowing, repayment, and expenditure are distinct stages; these are dated audit observations, not a current fraud finding.

documents.title: State of West Bengal v Baishakhi Bhattacharyya, 2025 INSC 437
documents.text: Supreme Court upheld cancellation of the entire school selection process with modifications, cited outsourcing and record-preservation failures, and expressly distinguished tainted from not-specifically-tainted candidates. This is a dated civil selection-process judgment, not a finding that every affected candidate committed a crime. Para 50 says observations and findings would not influence criminal proceedings. Subsequent implementation orders and fresh recruitment outcomes are not exhaustively tracked here; historical relief must not be presented as current employment status.

documents.title: REC model guidance for AMISP smart system metering
documents.text: DBFOOT service includes supply, installation, integration, operations and maintenance; payment is by operational meter-months and specified lump sums. Meter ownership remains with AMISP during the contract. Model terms are not evidence that a particular DISCOM adopted every clause. A filename version is not an independently established publication day. TOTEX lifecycle prices cannot be compared directly to meter hardware prices. Origin fetch HTTP 503; official indexed text reviewed.

documents.title: Cabinet approves AMRUT 2.0 till 2025–26
documents.text: City Water Balance Plans are intended to quantify source, demand, supply and service gaps, feeding city/state action plans. Approved programme design is not measured city-level achievement. Later extensions or revisions need separate dated orders.

documents.title: Chhattisgarh Samagra Shiksha 2025-26 revised PAB minutes
documents.text: Approved annual work plan: ₹232,029.17 lakh including ₹82,492.13 lakh spillover. Planned central share to be released: ₹112,900.28 lakh; corresponding state share ₹75,267.52 lakh. Supplementary ICT labs and smart classrooms approval: ₹14,133.80 lakh. Supersedes sections of earlier 9 May 2025 minutes; preserve version history. The section heading says Actual Release, but the line explicitly says to be released: classify as planned/approved, not actual disbursement. Opening balances and spillover make the approved plan different from fresh allocations. OCR affects table layout; use explicit prose figures and reconcile original PDF before bulk extraction. Origin PDF returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-06; preserve indexed-text access status and locate replacement archive before treating as live-verified.

documents.title: Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules, 2023 — G.S.R. 437(E)
documents.text: Requires daily remote smart-meter reading and daily consumer data access; inserts time-of-day tariff rules and advance display/notification requirements. Use the Gazette wording: commercial/industrial maximum demand more than 10 kW; some government summaries paraphrase this differently. National rules require the applicable State Commission tariff/supply-code instruments to establish a particular consumer bill. Commencement is publication in the Official Gazette; header issue is dated 14 June, while electronic Gazette identifier contains 15062023.

documents.title: National report on functionality assessment of tap connections, 2024
documents.text: Survey covered 19,812 Har Ghar Jal villages, 237,608 households, 761 districts and 34 states/UTs. Table 6 publishes separate regularity, quantity, tested-quality and minimum-of-three index percentages. Section 4.7 explicitly says the sampling design cannot identify the same household fulfilling all three parameters; the published functionality index takes their minimum. Table 6 household-quality assessment uses microbiological laboratory testing and on-site pH; source-water chemical testing is analysed separately in the report. Selected Har Ghar Jal villages are not all rural villages. Published minimum index is not the observed joint share of functional household supply. The Table 6 household-quality percentage does not establish full BIS chemical safety, including arsenic or fluoride; source-water chemical tests are a separate sample. Quantity and quality have different sampling units; do not combine as household intersection. Exact original publication day is unconfirmed; URL folder date is not used as publication date.

documents.title: CAG Karnataka Report No. 12 of 2025: implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission
documents.text: Section 3.3.1 records incomplete work in Hebbal, Shirahatti taluk, Gadag district during 2024 despite Har Ghar Jal reported status. Government responded in May 2025 that the elevated reservoir was completed by 8 April 2025, with 200 m pipeline and 20 FHTCs remaining before certification/trial run. Section 3.5 discusses 33 tenders worth ₹251.75 crore invited/awarded after 31 March 2024; Government cites timely administrative approvals and delays from non-participation and re-tendering. Sections 3.7.1–3.7.2 identify missing cross-system project/contractor keys and 9,342 first-call single-bid awards among 38,231 finalised works, with government response. Report sample is 28 villages in seven districts; it is not a statewide failure rate. Har Ghar Jal reported status and certified status differ. Audit period begins before requested window; Hebbal implementation findings from 2024 and response from 2025 are separately dated. No evidence of current 2026 conditions or individual guilt is inferred. Exact original publication day unconfirmed; direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 503. Section 3.5 distinguishes extended award deadlines: 15 March 2024 for in-village works and 31 March 2024 for multi-village schemes. The 33 flagged tenders were after the later date; no universal 31 March deadline is inferred.

documents.title: Kerala CAG audit, Chapter IV: implementation of schemes
documents.text: Audit reports 2,726 completed out of 5,318 JJM works as at November 2024. 122 of 342 surveyed beneficiaries reported no, limited or infrequent supply. Government response cites 21 lakh additional taps in four years and implementation constraints. Survey findings describe the audit sample, not all Kerala households. Part of the audited period precedes the requested 6 October 2021 window. Exact publication date is unconfirmed; 2025 report archive path is not assigned as a publication day. Direct original URL returned HTTP 503; Exa primary-document indexed extract was reviewed. Audit observations are not a finding of criminal intent and not proof the conditions continue in 2026.

documents.title: KKR and PSP invest in Lighthouse Learning
documents.text: Primary corporate announcement on 25 November 2025 says KKR-managed funds invested alongside new investor PSP Investments and KKR would continue holding a majority stake in Lighthouse Learning, an education services platform. No transaction amount disclosed in the primary announcement. Do not substitute media transaction estimates as primary-verified values. Equity in services platform is distinct from donations to schools, ownership of regulated educational trusts, or FCRA contributions. Presence is not proof investment proceeds were spent in every named city; Delhi NCR crosses administrative borders. Delhi-NCR presence is a regional label; it does not establish a school or spending location within Delhi's administrative boundary. Corporate self-disclosure documents what was announced; no government contract, donation quid pro quo, political control, or shareholding percentage is established.

documents.title: CAG landing record: PMJAY performance audit 11/2023
documents.text: Official metadata dates the PMJAY performance audit and defines its audited period. Publication within the recent window does not move historical claims into that window.

documents.title: CAG PMJAY 11/2023, Chapter V: claims management
documents.text: Paragraph 5.4 records ₹1.37 crore paid in 458 Andhra Pradesh cases and ₹3.61 crore in 1,080 Punjab cases for private-hospital procedures reserved for public hospitals. NHA cites temporary opening of public-reserved packages during COVID. Chapter also separates public-hospital use of claim revenue from private-hospital claim payments. Service claims are not hospital-construction tender values or private equity funding. Package, referral exception and treatment date must be reconciled before identifying an impermissible claim. Original PDF fetch returned HTTP 503; indexed original chapter text retained.

documents.title: Cabinet approval: PMJAY coverage for people aged 70 and above
documents.text: Approves coverage for all people aged 70 and above regardless of income; specifies separate top-up for already-covered families and choice conditions for certain public schemes. Scheme policy approval, not an Act of Parliament or proof of a hospital payment. Coverage ceiling is not actual expenditure; adoption and eligible hospital records remain necessary.

documents.title: PMJAY age-70 coverage expansion launch
documents.text: Records launch of the age-70 coverage expansion and Ayushman Vay Vandana Card. The ₹12,850 crore headline spans multiple launched, inaugurated and foundation-stone projects; do not assign it to the coverage expansion. State implementation mentioned in the historical speech is not a current all-state status ledger.

documents.title: Quota for EWS Seats in Private Unaided Schools — Lok Sabha Question 1260
documents.text: Provides sanctioned and reimbursed-to-school amounts under RTE for Karnataka for five years. FY 2025-26 sanctioned ₹156.10 crore and reimbursed ₹148.68 crore. Government says reimbursement is timely, based on information from the state. Describes 2018 Karnataka neighbourhood-school exemption. Including Bengaluru does not make this city-level funding. The table covers the reimbursement claim population; do not interpret as uniquely new entry-grade admissions without checking definitions. Sanctioned less reimbursed does not establish overdue obligations or misuse. Distinct from central releases to the state; do not sum with Samagra central share as independent money.

documents.title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
documents.text: Section 12(1)(c) provides entry-level admissions for eligible disadvantaged/weaker-section children of at least 25% in specified categories of schools. Section 12(2) provides private unaided school reimbursement capped at state per-child expenditure or actual charge, whichever is lower, with provisos for pre-existing free-education obligations. Not an unrestricted private-school capital grant. School eligibility, constitutional/applicability exclusions, neighbourhood rules and claims are determined by applicable law and state implementation. Statutory eligibility is not evidence of payment.

documents.title: Uttar Pradesh CAG 7/2025: DDUGJY and SAUBHAGYA
documents.text: Paragraph 3.3.4 attributes ₹46.27 crore paid for overlapping manpower/PMA work. The duplicate-connection headline is ₹26.65 crore; paragraphs 3.3.8–3.3.9 include grid and standalone-solar categories. Both responses and reported recovery progress accompany these historical findings. These are attributed audit conclusions, not criminal adjudications or current unrecovered loss. Audit period substantially predates the recent publication window. Chapter-only extraction lost body text; the full official report endpoint supplied readable indexed text. Original full-report binary returned HTTP 503; indexed primary text retained. Do not add the separately stated ₹4.41 crore standalone-solar duplicate category to the ₹26.65 crore headline: 3.3.8 listed amounts round to ₹22.24 crore, plus 3.3.9 ₹4.41 crore rounds to that headline.

documents.title: CAG landing record: UP electricity performance audit 7/2025
documents.text: Establishes the audit publication date and coverage through December 2022. Tabling date is not the date of the expenditure or government reply.

documents.title: UP CAG Compliance Audit-I 1/2023: incomplete Azamgarh KGBVs
documents.text: Paragraph 2.2 records ₹1.17 crore unfruitful expenditure on two incomplete KGBVs in Lalganj and Thekma; quality-check failures, revised estimates, and recovery/re-allotment concerns are detailed with government response. Historical sample of two buildings out of 15 sanctioned KGBVs; not all UP schools. Reconstruction and completion estimates are not additional paid expenditure. Original chapter fetch was refused with HTTP 403; full-report alternate returned 503. Only indexed primary text is archived.

documents.title: CAG UP register: Compliance Audit-I 1/2023
documents.text: Official register identifies the 2023 Compliance Audit-I report publication date. Index is metadata; detailed findings and replies come from paragraph 2.2.

documents.title: AGMARKNET commodity-wise, market-wise daily report
documents.text: Report separates price, arrivals or both and offers commodity and market discovery. Commodity list includes rice/wheat/pulses, vegetables and fruits. Daily report values and observation dates require explicit query/export validation before charting. No source farm or village origin can be inferred from market location. Missing reports are not zero arrivals; market unit and grade must be retained.

documents.title: Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Table 4 reports national rice, wheat and pulses area, production and yield for 2021–22 to 2023–24. Section 5.4.2 reports 2023–24 third advance horticulture estimates: vegetables 11.17 million ha, 205.80 million tonnes, 18.42 tonnes/ha. Section 5.4.6 records May 2024 training for farmers from named Nagaland villages and July 2024 horticulture-officer training in Shillong. Report is historical and mixes final, advance and cumulative series; retain each observation's own version and period. National crop totals cannot be allocated to states, cities or villages. Origin download returned HTTP 403; statements rely on official-domain indexed text. Exa extraction extended to 500,000 characters, selected sections reviewed. Village training examples do not establish village production, water access, funding receipt or programme impact.

documents.title: CAG Report 20 of 2023: FCI storage management and movement
documents.text: CAG section 3.4.3 found 10.55 lakh MT owned CAP storage vacant while additional storage was hired in Punjab/Haryana during RMS 2020–21/2021–22. CAG assessed ₹62.76 crore avoidable storage/supervision expenditure. FCI management said hiring anticipated a bumper paddy crop and finalized guaranteed-hiring tenders could not be cancelled without litigation; CAG rejected the explanation. Observed procurement/storage seasons partly precede 6 October 2021; do not label as current losses. Capacity figures are not foodgrain spoilage quantities; audit assessment is not a finding of criminal intent. Underlying ministry had not replied on this point according to the report; subsequent recovery/action was not established. Direct-origin request returned HTTP 503; official-domain indexed extract was reviewed through the relevant section.

documents.title: CAG: Haryana wheat procurement, storage and delivery to FCI
documents.text: CAG section 3.4.2 assessed ₹54.90 crore penalties leviable on transporters for lifting delays in RMS 2020/2021; says none were imposed. Department cited pandemic operating restrictions and efforts to maintain procurement; CAG said no State decision waived the penalties. Audit covered eight of Haryana's twenty-two districts and disclosed incomplete 2020 vehicle data. 2025 official archive and February 2025 follow-up support contemporary publication context, but exact publication date was not established. Audited transactions largely predate the requested five-year window; retain them as older-period findings disclosed in the window. Audit-calculated levy is not proven theft, a court judgment, money recovered or a current 2026 loss. Direct-origin PDF request returned HTTP 503; official-domain indexed text was read.

documents.title: Building resilient infrastructure for storage of food grains
documents.text: Reports 8,815 cold storages with 402.18 lakh MT capacity as of 30 June 2025. Reports 917.83 lakh MT covered/CAP central-pool storage capacity with FCI and state agencies as of 1 July 2025. Describes cold-chain, PACS and Kisan SAMPADA infrastructure; as of August 2025 eleven PACS pilot godowns in eleven states were completed. Capacity is not stock, annual throughput, uninterrupted operation or equal local access. Cold storage spans horticulture, dairy, meat and seafood; total cannot be attributed to vegetables alone. Announced, sanctioned, constructed and operational facilities require separate status; no complete village storage inventory verified. Kisan SAMPADA PMKSY is distinct from irrigation PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana.

documents.title: Second advance estimates of major agricultural crops, 2024–25
documents.text: Release describes estimate construction using state crop-area data, remote sensing, crop-weather review and crop-cutting experiments. Published quantities are an advance-estimate vintage, not final harvest outcomes. This March 2025 estimate is historical and superseded by later vintages; do not present as latest 2024–25 final output. Kharif, Rabi and annual quantities must be aligned; estimate revision is not automatically a reporting irregularity.

documents.title: Economic Survey 2025–26 Table 1.18: leading crop-producing states
documents.text: Official table lists the top three producing states by crop, including rice, wheat and total pulses. Rice: UP 20.76, Telangana 17.45, West Bengal 16.02 million tonnes; wheat: UP 35.65, MP 24.51, Punjab 17.99 million tonnes. Total pulses: MP 5.24, Maharashtra 5.04, Rajasthan 3.93 million tonnes. Top-three table is not an all-state crop inventory and absent states are not zero producers. Crop groups overlap with constituent crops; do not sum pulses and gram/tur or rice and total foodgrains. Cotton/jute table rows use million bales, not million tonnes; those rows were excluded from normalized observations.

documents.title: Department of Food and Public Distribution Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Department responsibilities span MSP procurement, movement, storage and distribution under food security policy. FCI and state agencies serve distinct procurement/storage/distribution roles. Quality-control cells and grain-analysis facilities monitor specifications and storage quality. Responsibilities and aggregate operations do not establish adequate access, quality or entitlements in every locality. PDS allocation, lifting/offtake, distribution and household receipt are different stages. Initial extract reviewed was capped at 18,000 characters; no complete stock series extracted.

documents.title: eNAM AGMARKNET market-price dashboard
documents.text: Dashboard supports state, district, APMC, commodity and date filters. Schema distinguishes arrivals, quantity traded, commodity variety, min/modal/max price, unit and observation date. Only schema and selectors were retrieved; no current price observation was verified. Mandi arrivals are flows through reporting markets, not local crop production, household availability or consumption. Modal prices are neither guaranteed MSP receipts nor complete retail food-price series.

documents.title: FCI operations dashboard: procurement, stocks, allocation and offtake
documents.text: Dashboard labels 36 states/UTs and 26 FCI regions. Fields distinguish allocation/offtake, paddy/wheat procurement, due/made payment, capacity, stock and utilization. Fetched snapshot lacks a reliable selected-date context and mixes day/progressive counters. Some displayed ratios exceed 100%; do not call fraud or shortage without denominator, period and system-status reconciliation. No dynamic amounts published as normalized observations.

documents.title: Rationalisation of Fertilizer Subsidy — Lok Sabha Q3255
documents.text: Answer says fertilizer subsidy is released to companies based on actual authenticated retail sales. Government states subsidy funds are not allocated or disbursed on a district- or state-wise basis, so that allocation data is not maintained. iFMS monitors movement, supply, dispatch, stock and allocation status. Do not invent state fertilizer subsidy amounts from national company payments or from quantities supplied. Subsidized sale, warehouse stock, agronomic need and farmer access are different measures. Published matrix extraction is malformed; financial values not normalized.

documents.title: ICAR Annual Report 2024–25: crop improvement and seed production
documents.text: Report highlights 524 notified/released field-crop varieties and hybrids, including 79 for abiotic stresses. Summary reports 106,397.6 quintals breeder seed produced against indent of 62,104.7 quintals, and 428,046 quintals quality seed including foundation, certified and truthfully labelled classes. ICAR reported output is not all-India commercial seed production or seed actually delivered to every farmer. Variety release, breeder-seed production, certification and retail seed availability are different stages. Do not promise stress resistance or yield without variety-specific adaptation recommendations.

documents.title: Progress made under PMKSY — Lok Sabha starred Q165
documents.text: Answer distinguishes irrigation potential created, command area developed and micro-irrigation coverage. Reports 114.60 lakh ha cumulative PDMC coverage since 2015–16. Reports 14,071 ha under PDMC in Dahod district and two watershed projects covering 15,785 ha; states no AIBP/HKKP project in Dahod Lok Sabha constituency. Dahod district and parliamentary constituency are not identical geographies; no-project finding is component-specific. Irrigation potential, actual water delivery and sustainably available water are not interchangeable. Programme totals cannot show effectiveness in a village; cumulative and three-year figures must remain separate.

documents.title: Drip and sprinkler irrigation through PMKSY — Lok Sabha Q2767
documents.text: PDMC moved from PMKSY to PM-RKVY from FY 2022–23. Government reports 96.97 lakh ha micro-irrigation coverage: 46.37 lakh ha drip and 50.60 lakh ha sprinkler. Assistance is 55% of unit cost for small/marginal farmers and 45% for others. Cumulative coverage begins before the requested five-year window and is labelled historical cumulative. Area covered is not measured water saved, crop yield impact or reliable current system operation. Do not confuse PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana with PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana, which shares the acronym PMKSY.

documents.title: Crop failure assistance: PMFBY premium support and claims
documents.text: Release separates government premium subsidy from claims paid under PMFBY and RWBCIS. Digiclaim module is described as operational for claims from Kharif 2022; crop-cutting experiments and technology-based yield estimation support assessment. Insurance premium subsidy is not identical to a farmer's claim payment or measured crop loss. Table extraction omits some row labels; no monetary rows from the malformed annexure were normalized. Claims depend on season, insured crop, notification, coverage, assessment and settlement cutoff; applications are not necessarily unique farmers.

documents.title: SATHI: seed lifecycle and traceability
documents.text: SATHI describes seed production, certification, licensing, inventory, sale and traceability across generations. Digital field inspections and laboratory workflows support certification. Portal describes capabilities, not universal adoption or verified seed quality for any village. A seed tag identifies a batch; certification does not guarantee yield in every climate.

documents.title: SATHI services and onboarded-state statistics
documents.text: Service page distinguishes registered area, processed/tested/certified quantities and seed sold. Page notes repeat tests can affect tested-versus-processed quantity comparisons. Fetched statistics contain unresolved template variables; no numeric seed stock or state coverage was extracted. Do not treat blank templates as zero or compare different processing stages as shrinkage.

documents.title: Household tap connections provided under AMRUT 2.0
documents.text: Official ULB table reports household tap connections provided under AMRUT 2.0. Selected city rows are retained with original table row and PDF page locators. Programme-provided connection count is not the city's total connections or coverage percentage. No city population denominator, daily availability or quality is inferred. Municipal jurisdiction must not be silently substituted for district or metropolitan area.

documents.title: Cabinet approves AMRUT 2.0 till 2025–26
documents.text: City Water Balance Plans are intended to quantify source, demand, supply and service gaps, feeding city/state action plans. Approved programme design is not measured city-level achievement. Later extensions or revisions need separate dated orders.

documents.title: Many Bengaluru apartments continue water conservation measures post the crisis period
documents.text: Resident associations and Bengaluru Apartments Federation describe continued conservation, rainwater harvesting and reuse after the acute crisis. Qualitative stakeholder reporting is not a representative household survey. Anecdotes about reuse do not establish drinking-water safety. Continued local tanker dependence does not establish uniform city conditions.

documents.title: Bengaluru after the water crisis: utility response and conservation
documents.text: Interview with BWSSB chairman describes tanker coordination, conservation and reuse responses to the 2024 shortage. Reported stakeholder perspective, not independently audited service data. Headline 'Day Zero' is not adopted as a verified citywide outage classification. Projections and uncorroborated numerical claims are not imported.

documents.title: CAG Karnataka Report No. 12 of 2025: implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission
documents.text: Section 3.3.1 records incomplete work in Hebbal, Shirahatti taluk, Gadag district during 2024 despite Har Ghar Jal reported status. Government responded in May 2025 that the elevated reservoir was completed by 8 April 2025, with 200 m pipeline and 20 FHTCs remaining before certification/trial run. Section 3.5 discusses 33 tenders worth ₹251.75 crore invited/awarded after 31 March 2024; Government cites timely administrative approvals and delays from non-participation and re-tendering. Report sample is 28 villages in seven districts; it is not a statewide failure rate. Har Ghar Jal reported status and certified status differ. Audit period begins before requested window; Hebbal implementation findings from 2024 and response from 2025 are separately dated. No evidence of current 2026 conditions or individual guilt is inferred. Exact original publication day unconfirmed; direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 503.

documents.title: Kerala CAG audit, Chapter IV: implementation of schemes
documents.text: Audit reports 2,726 completed out of 5,318 JJM works as at November 2024. 122 of 342 surveyed beneficiaries reported no, limited or infrequent supply. Government response cites 21 lakh additional taps in four years and implementation constraints. Survey findings describe the audit sample, not all Kerala households. Part of the audited period precedes the requested 6 October 2021 window. Exact publication date is unconfirmed; 2025 report archive path is not assigned as a publication day. Direct original URL returned HTTP 503; Exa primary-document indexed extract was reviewed. Audit observations are not a finding of criminal intent and not proof the conditions continue in 2026.

documents.title: Dynamic Groundwater Resources Assessment, 2025
documents.text: Annual recharge is 448.52 BCM; annual extractable resources 407.75 BCM; annual extraction 247.22 BCM; national extraction stage 60.63%. Among 6,762 assessed units, 4,946 safe, 758 semi-critical, 201 critical, 730 over-exploited and 127 saline units are reported. Safe is a groundwater extraction-stage category, not a drinking-water-quality guarantee. Units generally mean blocks/tehsils/talukas/mandals, not individual villages. National mean cannot describe every aquifer; extraction includes irrigation, domestic and industrial uses. All-state numeric groundwater table was not recovered in this workstream.

documents.title: CGWB publications repository
documents.text: Repository offers state/district and aquifer resources, groundwater quality and resource assessments. Discovery index only; report dates, coverage and assessment units need document-level verification. Direct origin retrieval returned HTTP 503; indexed text was available.

documents.title: Government eProcurement System: advanced tender search
documents.text: Official search filters support organisation, tender ID, work category and dates. Discovery link is not a list of water awards or executed contracts. CAPTCHA and interactive filtering limit automatic retrieval. Tender notice, corrigendum, cancellation, award and payment are separate records; no tender counts or award amounts are invented.

documents.title: GeM: all bids
documents.text: Official portal provides bid discovery and warns new or modified bids may take time to appear. No hydrated bid results were retrieved. Procurement discovery is not evidence of an award, payment or misconduct. Water procurement must be filtered and individual dated documents reviewed.

documents.title: Water Resources Information System: India-WRIS
documents.text: India-WRIS brings together water-resource spatial and temporal information for assessment and planning. Official linked platform is https://indiawris.gov.in/wris/#/. Station and basin observations are not measurements for every village. Check station, parameter, season, datum and spatial boundaries before combining with supply data.

documents.title: Assessment of functionality of household tap water connections provided under JJM
documents.text: Release reports 98.1% connections available, 86.5% working, 80.2% adequate quantity, 83.6% regularity and 76% tested water quality in surveyed villages. Certification requires a Gram Sabha resolution after work completion reporting. Use the underlying report's sample definitions and minimum-index method. Published percentages are not universal village or household safety claims.

documents.title: JJM Dashboard: reported and certified Har Ghar Jal
documents.text: Administrative household tap-connection monitoring and separate reported/certified Har Ghar Jal statuses. Official state, district and village discovery routes are available. A connection is not continuous safe supply. Unhydrated dashboard zero placeholders were not imported. Live household/village denominators may be reconciled; snapshots must retain dates.

documents.title: National report on functionality assessment of tap connections, 2024
documents.text: Survey covered 19,812 Har Ghar Jal villages, 237,608 households, 761 districts and 34 states/UTs. Table 6 publishes separate regularity, quantity, tested-quality and minimum-of-three index percentages. Section 4.7 explicitly says the sampling design cannot identify the same household fulfilling all three parameters; the published functionality index takes their minimum. Table 6 household-quality assessment uses microbiological laboratory testing and on-site pH; source-water chemical testing is analysed separately in the report. Selected Har Ghar Jal villages are not all rural villages. Published minimum index is not the observed joint share of functional household supply. The Table 6 household-quality percentage does not establish full BIS chemical safety, including arsenic or fluoride; source-water chemical tests are a separate sample. Quantity and quality have different sampling units; do not combine as household intersection. Exact original publication day is unconfirmed; URL folder date is not used as publication date.

documents.title: Format J3: tap connections in villages with piped water supply
documents.text: 34 rural state/UT rows provide rural households, balance household tap connections and households with tap connections in PWS villages. The published total is 586,054 villages, 1,935.52 lakh rural households and 1,589.93 lakh households with tap connections in PWS villages. Household figures are rounded to 0.01 lakh. PWS-village households and all-rural households are different denominators. Administrative connections do not establish regularity, quantity or water quality. Delhi and Chandigarh are absent; no zeros are imputed. Exa returned a dated 27 July snapshot; it is not relabelled an October count.

documents.title: JJM Citizen Corner: village information
documents.text: Village search supports water-quality, piped-water-supply, community management and certification discovery. Discovery route only; no individual village values were retrieved from this portal. Village names must be resolved with state/district/subdistrict identifiers.

documents.title: National Water Data Portal: NWIC water data
documents.text: Water-data discovery spans quantity, quality, use, planning, climate and related infrastructure. Portal availability does not imply uniform geographic coverage, freshness or village granularity. Dataset-specific metadata and access terms must be checked.

documents.title: Water quality management under JJM
documents.text: BIS 10500 is the drinking-water quality benchmark. Arsenic/fluoride affected habitations may receive interim community water purification provision at 8–10 litres per capita per day for drinking and cooking while permanent schemes are implemented. Interim drinking/cooking volume is not the full 55 LPCD household service benchmark. Policy provision is not proof of installation or safe operation in any locality.

documents.title: WQMIS public reports
documents.text: Public report routes include infrastructure/delivery points, remedial action, laboratory capacity, parameters and field-test-kit testing. Only report index was retrieved; no contamination counts or clean-water rates are inferred. Unhydrated dashboard zero placeholders are missing data, not absence of contamination. Sample time, water point, contaminant and retest/remedial action are required for exposure assessment.

documents.title: Cuttack block-wise Agromet Advisory, July 1–5, 2025
documents.text: Expired block-level advisory links forecast rain to rice nursery drainage, irrigation timing and crop stages. Athagad and Badamba sections explicitly say forecast period from today 08:30 IST to July 6, 2025 08:30 IST. General advice discusses draining excess water from rice nurseries, delaying irrigation and weather-dependent farm operations. The bulletin separately dates NDVI to June 12–18 and SPI to May 29–June 25, 2025. Historical expired advice, not present planting or chemical-use instructions. Issue clock time is not stated; 08:30 is the forecast-period boundary, not necessarily issuance time. Block advisory cannot be relabelled as village field conditions or proof that a pest/disease occurred.

documents.title: BWSSB chairman interview on drinking-water reserves and peripheral shortages
documents.text: Utility response distinguishes basin water available for drinking from shortages in areas reliant on borewells. BWSSB chairman said 110 villages relied on borewells and groundwater levels had fallen. He said basin storage would be sufficient for drinking needs until monsoon and urged treated-water use for other purposes. Utility official's attributed assessment is not independent verification of every household's supply. Different dates, service boundaries and drinking/non-drinking scopes must be aligned before comparing with other estimates. An expectation about future supply in March 2024 is an expired historical statement.

documents.title: Families, schools and hospitals describe Bengaluru water shortage
documents.text: Local reporting documents reported interruptions, tanker dependence and pressure on schools and a hospital. Residents in Krishnanapalya describe shortened Cauvery supply. Inspire Public School in Thanisandra and Sai Hospital in Hegde Nagar report dry borewells and dependence on tankers. Article explicitly says a reported 1,500-foot borewell-depth claim could not be independently verified. Interviews are qualitative community evidence and are not a representative city survey. Keep named institution and neighbourhood scope; reported tanker prices need delivery date/volume/radius matching. Do not reuse the unverified borewell depth as a measurement.

documents.title: Bengaluru facing 500 MLD shortfall, Chief Minister says
documents.text: Reporting attributes a quantified water deficit and borewell stress to Karnataka's Chief Minister. Chief Minister is quoted giving demand 2,600 MLD, Cauvery supply 1,450 MLD, groundwater supply 650 MLD and shortfall 500 MLD. He said 6,900 of 14,000 government borewells had dried and named outer areas without Cauvery service as affected. Attributed official statements reported by news; not independently audited measurements. A city-wide average cannot establish supply at a selected ward or village. Historical March 2024 snapshot, not current 2026 supply.

documents.title: CWC Flood Forecast portal
documents.text: Official source discovery for river-level and inflow forecasts. Fetched page identifies itself as CWC Flood Forecast. JavaScript portal returned no station observations, issue times or validity data to the text fetch. No current flood status or live alert can be inferred from this record.

documents.title: CWC reservoir storage bulletin archive: 2024 snapshots
documents.text: Official directory lists dated live-storage reports for 150 monitored reservoirs. Visible index includes 21 March, 28 March, 25 April and 13 June 2024 bulletins. Page text says last updated 14 June 2024. Archive snapshot is stale relative to October 2026; this is not live storage. Underlying reservoir PDFs were not individually fetched; no reservoir volume is asserted. Monitored reservoirs are not a census of every local tank, village source or groundwater aquifer.

documents.title: Manual for Drought Management, December 2016
documents.text: Government manual provides historical drought-monitoring and response methodology. Title page identifies December 2016 and the Government of India agriculture department. Manual concerns monitoring, drought declaration, relief and mitigation. Outside 2021-10-06 to 2026-10-06 evidence window; include only as clearly marked background. Fetched from an intergovernmental disaster-information mirror, not the original ministry host. Only opening portion fetched; current amendments and applicable state rules must be checked before operational use.

documents.title: Statement on the Climate of India during 2025
documents.text: National climate statement with regional rainfall differences and documented extreme-weather events. All-India annual rainfall is reported as 1,274 mm and 110% of the 1971–2020 long-period average. Southwest monsoon rainfall is reported as 127% of LPA for Northwest India and 80% for East & Northeast India, illustrating why national surplus does not rule out regional shortfall. National and homogeneous-region aggregates do not establish city/village conditions. Document says extreme-weather casualties use media and disaster-management reports; avoid treating every casualty as a direct instrument measurement.

documents.title: Drought Condition Assessment: September and June–September 2023
documents.text: IMD combines SPI, SPEI and aridity anomaly indicators in a district assessment. Summary reports dry/arid classifications from multiple drought indices. District names and indicator-specific tables are provided; classifications are historical. Publication date not stated in fetched text; period is not a publication date. Extracted text includes a September 2022 table caption within the 2023 report and an implausible 30 states / 11 UTs phrase. Reconcile against original pages before loading numerical tables. Meteorological indicators do not establish household tap reliability or an administrative drought declaration.

documents.title: IMD press release: May 23, 2024 weather outlook
documents.text: Archived bulletin demonstrates timestamped forecast evidence, including cyclone and heatwave expectations. Issued May 23, 2024 at 1410 IST. Subject forecasts a cyclonic storm approaching Bangladesh/adjoining West Bengal by May 26 evening and heatwave conditions over named regions during the next five days. Expired forecast; it is neither evidence that all predicted impacts occurred nor a current alert. Different hazards have different valid windows. No single precise expiry time is stated for the whole release. Use observed follow-up bulletins to evaluate forecast outcomes.

documents.title: Monthly Hydroclimate Summary Bulletin: June 2026
documents.text: District hydroclimate bulletin reports SPI, SPEI, aridity, rainfall and temperature for June 2026. The document explicitly identifies June 2026 and separates SPI, SPEI and AAI. It provides maps and region-wise district classifications. Undated mutable bulletin URL; retrieved content is June 2026, not October conditions. Extracted SPI region rows and All India extreme-wet totals do not reconcile. Verify PDF/table extraction before any district count metric. Rainfall and hydroclimate classifications alone are not village drought declarations.

documents.title: Rainfall Statistics of India – 2024
documents.text: Official compilation of monthly, seasonal and annual 2024 rainfall. Report identifier is ESSO/MoES/IMD/HS/Rainfall Report/02(2025)/66. Annual map reports all-India rainfall 1,206.6 mm against 1,160.0 mm normal, a rounded 4% departure. Publication year is 2025 in report identifier; exact publication day is not stated in extracted opening pages. Fetched URL contains a session token and may require replacing with a stable official locator. Only opening pages were fetched; no district observations have been transcribed.

documents.title: State-wise Annual Climate Statements, 2021–2024
documents.text: Discovery route to state climate statements covering temperature, rainfall, SPI and extreme-weather impacts. Portal says the 2021 state climate statements were first prepared in 2022. Selectors show 2021–2024 and state names. Discovery index, not an ingested state-level dataset. 2021 annual documents partly precede the requested window beginning 2021-10-06; finer-period records are needed to filter strictly. No individual state report values were extracted in this workstream.

documents.title: IIT Madras assessment of Ennore oil spill, filed with TNPCB report at NGT
documents.text: Technical assessment describes flood-driven industrial oil contamination of waterways and adjoining residential areas. Report maps contamination zones and says affected open wells are groundwater sources. Executive summary calls for remediation and further assessment of prolonged exposure via air, water and fish. Technical report filed in proceedings is not a final court finding or a present water-quality clearance. Avoid adding oil mass and oily-sludge mass as comparable quantities; report itself uses different estimates and discusses uncertainty. March 2024 is the report month; exact filing/publication day not established.

documents.title: NRSC Michaung inundation map: 7 December 2023
documents.text: Rapid satellite inundation mapping provides a historical footprint with explicit uncertainty. Table 2 totals 148,360 hectares of mapped inundation/standing water over listed districts. Report requests field feedback and says no ground verification was done. Preliminary rapid map; inundation can include rain accumulation or water in paddy fields. Satellite scale, resolution, date and interpretation limit conclusions; mapped water is not automatically crop loss or unsafe drinking water. Acquisition time zone is unstated; do not append IST without confirmation.

documents.title: Tamil Nadu Gazette: cyclone- and flood-affected districts declaration
documents.text: G.O. 604 formally declares named cyclone- and flood-affected districts in December 2023. Order declares Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu and Kancheepuram cyclone affected. It declares six southern districts flood affected and describes damage to crops and water-supply infrastructure. Historical declaration is not a present warning. Rainfall quantities in the order require station/aggregation interpretation before numerical reuse; only declaration and described impacts used here.

documents.title: Lok Sabha AU241: Deendayal Divyangjan Rehabilitation Scheme
documents.text: Department supplies district and named special-school NGO release figures, beneficiary counts and state grant tables. Release is not a utilisation certificate or independently verified service outcome. The dash for FY2025-26 is preserved as a dash; it does not prove closure, fraud or zero services. The named NGO is tied to Keonjhar Lok Sabha constituency in the source; no district or town location is inferred. Annexure II lists AGP recipients without recipient-level amounts; these must not inherit DDRS table totals. Original PDF fetched with HTTP 200 and SHA-256 archived.

documents.title: CAG Jharkhand Report 3/2023: Direct Benefit Transfer, Chapter 6 e-Kalyan
documents.text: Audit of the scholarship portal identifies doubtful ₹40.31 lakh linked to differing UID entries and absent validation controls. Official report catalogue 119516 establishes tabling on 21 December 2023; June 2023 signatures are not publication dates. Doubtful grant entries are not adjudicated fraud and do not establish every student’s intent. Audit 2017-18 to July 2020 includes older background; government observations remained unanswered in the retained chapter after referral in October 2022. Direct original PDF returned HTTP 503; indexed original-document text archived. Original-site availability is not asserted.

documents.title: CAG Kerala Report 3/2024: pre- and post-matric scholarships
documents.text: The audit follows scholarship instructions, application approval, bank rejection and money returned to treasury, showing why payment initiated is not payment received. Four sampled districts: Kollam, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Wayanad; 144 institutions. The e-grantz data snapshot was obtained in June 2022; subsequent payment updates were not included in analysis. Transaction counts are not necessarily unique students; rejected money returned to government is not an established embezzlement amount. Direct original PDF returned HTTP 503; indexed original-document text archived. Original-site availability is not asserted.

documents.title: Lok Sabha AU969: Mission Shakti implementation and releases
documents.text: Scheme release tables explicitly explain that Uttar Pradesh PMMVY received no fresh release because sufficient funds remained in its Single Nodal Agency account. Central release is distinct from state spending or beneficiary payment. Reasons for one state’s zero release must not be applied to another state without its own footnote. The source’s service/impact descriptions are government reports, not independent outcome validation. Original PDF fetched with HTTP 200 and SHA-256 archived.

documents.title: CAG Madhya Pradesh Report 8/2024: Take Home Ration compliance audit
documents.text: Final report examines beneficiary verification and take-home-ration supply during 2018-21, including the December 2022 government rebuttal. The final audit replaces reliance on a 2022 draft reported in the prior NGO corpus. Supply value, cash paid, unpaid bills and estimated avoidable expenditure are different stages; they must not be added. The retained long extract is capped at 500,000 characters; the decisive THR section and response are fully present. Direct original PDF returned HTTP 503; indexed original-document text archived. Original-site availability is not asserted.

documents.title: CAG Report 10/2023: National Social Assistance Programme
documents.text: National pension audit separates diversion of administrative publicity funds from short-payment of entitled pensions; December 2022 Ministry replies retained. Audit fieldwork covered 179 districts, 358 blocks, 699 Gram Panchayats and 8,461 surveyed beneficiaries; selected-district findings are not whole-population estimates. Audit period precedes the recent five-year window; the report and response are recent evidence about historical delivery. Direct original PDF returned HTTP 503; indexed original-document text archived. Original-site availability is not asserted.

documents.title: CAG Odisha Report 9/2025: POSHAN implementation, Chapter II ICDS
